name: Stride Basics Mesh Runner
description: A no-frills breathable mesh trainer in grey, white, or black. Lightweight knit upper, foam midsole, rubber outsole with basic tread. The kind of shoe that gets worn to work, to the market, and to bed when you're too tired to take them off.
functionality: Minimal cushion-adjust dial at heel — three settings. Otherwise purely mechanical.
what_it_says: You buy what works. No frills, no statement.
story_hooks: The cushion dial is stuck on max — the previous owner glued it there after a knee injury.
A pair of these found at a crime scene are the only lead connecting a witness to the wrong neighborhood.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian low-profile sneaker with a minimal silhouette. The mesh upper creates an airy, almost skeletal appearance with visible weave patterns. Sits close to the foot with a subtle forward lean, designed for perpetual motion. The overall impression is no-nonsense functionality—clean lines, zero ornamentation.
physical_description.fit: Snug through the midfoot with a relaxed toe box. The knit upper conforms to foot shape without compression. Collar sits at natural ankle height. Breaking-in period is minimal; immediate comfort is the design philosophy.
physical_description.primary_material: Breathable mesh knit upper (likely recycled poly-blend), EVA foam midsole, vulcanized rubber outsole with carbon-black coloring
physical_description.texture: Mesh has a slightly rough, permeable hand-feel with visible grid structure. Midsole is soft and compressible. Outsole tread is shallow but defined, waffle-pattern. Overall tactile impression: lightweight and aerated.
physical_description.color_scheme: Monochromatic palette—grey, white, or black. Grey is most common (neutral, hides wear). Minimal contrast; midsole may be slightly off-white or grey. No branding colors or accent stitching.
physical_description.closures: Standard lace closure with flat, utilitarian laces. Grommet eyelets are plastic-reinforced. Optional friction-fit style exists for quick on-off.
distinctive_features: Minimal tongue with integrated heel tab
Mesh upper extends to toe cap with no leather reinforcement
Visible foam midsole edge with slight yellowing after wear
Shallow tread pattern designed for pavement, not terrain
Worn sock-liner often visible from constant use
Stride Basics logo is understated—small printed mark on tongue or heel
No cushioning bumps or visible tech—completely flat profile
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 working class. Affordable, functional, zero aspirational value. Not poverty-tier salvage, but deliberately designed for people who can't afford to care about fashion.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by couriers, service workers, market vendors, and anyone navigating the GLMZ on foot. The shoe of people in motion—delivery runners, nurses doing 12-hour shifts, gig workers between jobs. Signals 'I have places to be' rather than 'look at me.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in within a week. Mesh darkens at stress points. Midsole develops visible creasing. Laces fray. Outsole shows pavement scuffs within days. After 6 months: heel tab worn soft, insole compressed to body-heat contours, minor mesh tears at toe. Owner usually replaces rather than repairs.

image_prompt: Overhead product shot of grey mesh runner on dark concrete, harsh fluorescent light casting sharp shadows. Close-up detail of worn mesh texture and rubber outsole. Second angle: shoe on foot of tired courier in dimly-lit GLMZ transit station, feet barely leaving ground, laces slightly loose. Neutral color grading with slight cyan undertones. Urban, unglamorous, lived-in aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
